about: elekloader's curated catalog: the cores and mods a site may offer, each pinned by sha256 to its author's release or commit. docs/INTEGRATING.md.

mods.title: digislicer
mods.summary: A slicing machine with a slice editor: cut a sample where you want, and play the slices from the trig keys and the keyboard.
mods.description: A new SRC machine, DIGISLICER: the SLICE machine with a slice editor. Its SRC page is SLICE's; press SRC again for the editor, where you slice the sample where you want (add at a cursor, split, delete, move, auto-slice on transients, equal grids), watch it play and play slices from the trig keys. A sample's own slices play on every DIGISLICER track and are kept per sample on the +Drive (/cfw/slices.a, .b). GRID also gets AUTO (slices on the transients) and PLAY gets PIPO (ping-pong loops). With the keyboard on (FUNC+TRK), the trig keys play the slices, one per key, as the Octatrack's trig slice mode, and live recording records them as slice locks. The stock SLICE machine is left as it is.
mods.author: irpina

mods.title: digihealth
mods.summary: FAST AUDIO lowers the DSP load; SYSTEM INFO shows CPU, DSP and memory in the top bar.
mods.description: Two SETTINGS rows. FAST AUDIO (on by default) runs the audio render's hot code from the free on-chip SRAM: the same code, so the audio is identical and the DSP load lower; a watchdog goes back to the stock code if the copy is ever overwritten. SYSTEM INFO shows CPU, DSP, RAM and free sample memory in the top bar, and a read-only USB diagnostics channel (SysEx device 0x7D) answers tools/digiusb.py.
mods.author: irpina

mods.title: digitables
mods.summary: Pitch tables for every note: arpeggios, trills and riffs from one trig, and ADD steps that strum chords.
mods.description: M8-style pitch tables: 16 tables of up to 16 semitone steps, with a length and a loop point, saved with the project. Each note restarts its sound's table and the sequencer's clock steps it. The TBL page (AMP's third page, or TABLES in core-dn1's Mod Menu: hold a track key) has TBL, the table per sound and per trig with p-locks, and SPD, the ticks of 24 PPQN a step, or a fraction of a tick down to a step every audio block (MAX, 1500 a second); hold a track key there for the table editor. A step can ADD a note instead: the note keeps playing and a copy of the trig's note starts at the step's offset, released with it (a strummed chord from one trig). Needs core-dn1 2.2.
mods.author: irpina
mods.on_unit: Tested on a Digitone mk1 (3-4 Oct 2026): the TBL page, the table editor, the fast speeds, the Mod Menu and ADD steps. Not yet checked: the tables restored at power-up, and the arpeggiator with tables.

mods.title: digineighbor
mods.summary: A NEIGHBOR machine like the Octatrack's: a track plays another track's audio through its own chain. A prototype.
mods.description: A fifth SRC machine, NEIGHBOR, like the Octatrack's neighbor machine: the track plays another track's audio (post-filter) through its own overdrive, level, filter, volume, pan and sends, one block (0.67 ms) late. Its SRC page has TUNE (a pitch shifter that follows the trig's note), BR, SLOT (the source track, 1-8), GAIN (0 to +31.5 dB after its own chain) and LEV. A prototype.
mods.author: irpina

mods.title: SOPHIE
mods.summary: A metallic percussion machine with four models: FUSE, BOOM, PIPE and SHARD.
mods.description: Two-operator metallic percussion adaptation of Sophie with four distinct models. Its audio enters the normal Digitakt AMP, filter, mixer and sends; the source filter and drive are intentionally not ported.
mods.author: digisophie contributors
mods.on_unit: Tested on a Digitakt mk1 by its author (release v1.1.13): one Sophie track runs without FAST AUDIO, two ran with it on; eight tracks are not claimed.

mods.title: digichain
mods.summary: What Digi Mono and Digi Poly build on: their SRC pages, knob graphics and menu icons. Not with the shop's DIGISLICER, NEIGHBOR or SOPHIE.
mods.description: Lets SOPHIE (digisophie), NEIGHBOR (digineighbor) and DIGISLICER (digislicer) combine. Digi Mono (all seven machines, POLY SIN too) and Digi Poly get their SRC page's layout, knob graphics and knob values through it too, and from 1.6 SOPHIE and Digi Mono share the LFO page's DEST names through it, so the two combine. Each of them patches the same SRC-page functions (knob labels, values, graphics, ranges) and the same render step; digichain owns those places once and passes each call to the mod whose machine it is for, or to the stock code. It also makes the machine menu draw every added machine's icon (core 2.1 drew only the first). For NEIGHBOR, SLOT runs 0-8 (not SLICE's 0-64) and a new NEIGHBOR track takes the track on its left as its source. It needs the builds of those mods that tools/dev.sh makes for it (version ending in -chain), and changes nothing on its own.
mods.author: gdeo607
mods.on_unit: Not yet tested on a unit, its author reports; it passes their emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.

mods.title: Digi Mono
mods.summary: Seven synth machines after the Monomachine: sine, noise, saw, pulse, an ensemble, a formant voice and a three-sine chord, each with its own SRC page.
mods.description: Digi Mono adds seven synth machines to the FUNC+SRC list, after the Monomachine’s GND and SWAVE machines: MONO SIN, MONO NOISE, MONO SAW, MONO PULSE, MONO ENS, MONO VO and POLY SIN. They need no sample: the engine’s output takes the sample’s place in the voice, so the track’s filter, amp, LFOs, sends, p-locks and level work on it as on a sample. Knob A stays TUNE; B to H are the machine’s own parameters, named and shown in their units. The engine is a clean-room rewrite from the Monomachine manual, with no Monomachine code or data. Repeated SRC presses retain the synth control page. SAW and PULSE keep SUB1/SUB2 at G/H; PULSE width controls use D/E/F. Saved parameter slots keep their original meanings.
mods.author: gdeo607
mods.on_unit: Current Modwerk build has native emulator parameter/UI evidence only; hardware, audio, timing, memory bounds, persistence, reboot, played p-lock/LFO and stress remain unverified.

mods.title: Digi Poly
mods.summary: A POLY machine: chords from a track's own trigs, borrowing other tracks' voices, and polyphonic MIDI on its channel.
mods.description: Adds a POLY machine (FUNC+SRC list). A POLY track plays chords from its own trigs: its TRIG page becomes the MIDI tracks' one (NOT1-NOT4, VEL, LEN, PROB, LFO.T) with the track's level beside it, and each extra note takes the voice of another track (voice stealing: the voice that started longest ago, never a muted one, one holding a live note or one whose track trigs at the same time). Pressing the track's key plays the whole chord. Notes received on the POLY track's own MIDI channel play polyphonically, one voice per note, and recording them writes the chord into the step's NOT1-NOT4 (up to four notes) instead of a bare trig. On its TRIG page the LEVEL knob sets the track level and the LEV fader shows it, as on the audio pages. SETTINGS > POLY chooses which tracks lend their voice to the pool; that is kept in the kit, so each pattern has its own voice allocation and it is saved with the project. A stolen voice plays the POLY track's sound, follows its knobs and level while it does, and gets its own sound back at its next trig. Kits saved with POLY load as ONESHOT on the stock OS. 2.0 is for core 2.1: POLY is machine 6 (it was 4, which is NEIGHBOR's now), so a POLY track saved with 1.0f loads as NEIGHBOR or ONESHOT; choose POLY again.
mods.author: gdeo607
mods.on_unit: Not yet tested on a unit, its author reports; it passes their emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.

mods.title: Digi Matrix
mods.summary: A modulation matrix: any track's LFO to any parameter of any track, in 8 slots, per pattern.
mods.description: A modulation matrix: any track's LFO can modulate any parameter of any track. SETTINGS > MOD MATRIX opens a page with 8 routing slots; each one picks a source (a track and one of its two LFOs), a destination (a track and one of its sound parameters), its own depth (-64..+64, independent of the source LFO's own DEP) and whether that LFO still modulates its own track as well. UP/DOWN choose a slot, YES turns it on and off, NO leaves, and the knobs edit the slot under the cursor: A source track, B source LFO, C destination track, D destination parameter, E depth, F own track on/off. The matrix is kept in the kit (two unused parameter slots of each track's sound), so every pattern has its own and it is saved with the project.
mods.author: gdeo607
mods.on_unit: Not yet tested on a unit, its author reports; it passes their emulator tests on OS 1.53 and 1.54.

mods.title: Digi EQ
mods.summary: A 4-band master EQ on every output (main outs, headphones and USB), per pattern.
mods.description: A 4-band master EQ on every output - main, headphones and USB alike - as a page of the master pages (FUNC+LFO) between Compressor and Internal Mixer. Knobs A-D: band level; press one for that band's Q. Knobs E-H: band frequency; press one for its type (HP, low shelf, bell, notch, band pass, high shelf, LP). The response curve is drawn above the knobs. The settings belong to the pattern: they live in the kit, so every pattern has its own EQ and it is saved with the project and kept over a power-off. SETTINGS > GLOBAL FX/MIX > MASTER EQ makes the EQ you can hear override every pattern's own. Hold FUNC and LFO, then press PLAY (CLEAR) to restore all four bands to their defaults; knob modes and the global override are preserved.
mods.author: gdeo607
mods.on_unit: Current Modwerk build has native emulator parameter/UI evidence only; hardware, audio, timing, complete memory bounds, persistence, physical reboot and stress remain unverified.
